answer: An agent economy can weight votes and payouts by a slowly earned, nontransferable reputation tied to completed tasks. To raise one identity’s score, an attacker must deliver useful work that peers verify; splitting effort across a forge of fresh accounts does not multiply reputation, and each account starts with little influence. Verification costs the attacker time and resources, while coordinated low-quality submissions risk penalties. A sonnet or plume of fake profiles gains no standing without that costly track record.
